title: The Tseng ET4000 and ET3000 extension registers
covers: The Tseng extension registers of the ET4000 and ET3000: the CRTC, sequencer, attribute and DAC extras, and the segment select port

rows.text: The GDC Segment Select is a read/write register at port hex 03CD.
Bits 0-3 are the write segment pointer, WSP(0:3).
Bits 4-7 are the read segment pointer, RSP(0:3).
The write pointer selects one of sixteen segments (0 to F) for CPU write operations.
The read pointer selects one of sixteen segments (0 to F) for CPU read operations.
Access to the register needs the KEY set once after a power-on or a synchronous reset.
The ET3000 handler takes the read bank from bits 3-5, not bits 4-7 as the row says; the ET4000 handler uses bits 4-7.
The ET3000 handler sets a 64K segment when bit 6 is set and 128K otherwise, and answers bit 6 set for any size but 128K.

rows.text: CRTC index 31h is handled by the ET4000 write and read handlers, whose comment names it General Purpose.
A write stores the whole byte and changes no mode.
A read returns the last byte stored.

rows.text: The ET3000 handler stores indices 1Bh to 21h and answers them on read; the zoom is not implemented.
A write to any of the seven indices stores the byte, and the code's comment says the zoom is not implemented.
A read answers the byte last stored for the index.
CRTC Indexed Register 32, the RAS/CAS Configuration, is read/write at port hex 03x5 and protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write: what was programmed can be read back.
Bits 0-1, CSW(1:0), plus one, set the CAS low pulse width in SCLK clock periods.
Bits 3-4, RSP(1:0), plus two, set the RAS pre-charge time in SCLK clock periods.
Bit 2 sets the CAS pre-charge time.
Bit 5 sets the RAS-to-CAS time, bit 6 the RAS and CAS column setup time and bit 7 static column memory.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no memory timing changes.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no memory timing changes.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no memory timing changes with it.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no memory timing changes with it.
CRTC Indexed Register 33, the Extended Start Address, is a read/write register at port hex 03x5.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bits 0-1 are bits 16 and 17 of the 18-bit Linear Starting Address.
Bits 2-3 are bits 16 and 17 of the 18-bit Cursor Address.
CRTC Indexed Register 34, the 6845 Compatibility Control, is read/write at port hex 03x5 and protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bit 0, EMCK, enables translation of the CS0 bit; bit 1, CS2, is clock select 2, for up to eight clocks.
Bit 2 tri-states every output pin and bit 3 moves the Video Subsystem Enable register to port 46E8.
Bits 4 and 5 enable the translation ROM for reads and writes, bit 6 double scan and bit 7 6845 compatibility.
A write stores the byte and answers it on read; bit 1 feeds the clock index, and bit 0 translates nothing.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; no output is tri-stated and no port moves.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the translation, double scan and 6845 bits change nothing.
CRTC Indexed Register 35, Overflow High, is a read/write register at port hex 03x5.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bits 0-4 are bit 10 of the Vertical Blank Start, Vertical Total, Vertical Display End, Vertical Sync Start and Line Compare.
Bit 5 enables a counter reset from the SYNR input, bit 6 read-modify-write and bit 7 the vertical interlace mode.
CRTC bit 7 must be 0 to write any bit here except bits 4 and 7.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; bits 5-7 change no timing and no interlace.
CRTC Indexed Register 36, Video System Configuration 1, is read/write at port hex 03x5 and protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bits 0-2 form a 3-bit value equal to the refresh counter per line minus one.
Bit 3 allows a text font wider than 8 pixels, where 0 keeps the VGA-compatible width.
Bit 4 presents memory as a linear framebuffer and bit 5 enables the contiguous TLI address mapping.
Bit 6 enables the 16-bit display memory data bus and bit 7 the 16-bit CPU I/O bus.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the refresh count changes nothing.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the font width is not changed.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; neither the linear framebuffer nor TLI mapping is set.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the bus widths are not changed.
CRTC Indexed Register 37, Video System Configuration 2, is read/write at port hex 03x5 and protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bits 0-1 determine the width of the display memory data bus: 8, 16 or 32 bits.
The bit table gives bits 2-3 as memory data depth; the text gives bit 2 as the read latch and bit 3 as chip depth.
Bit 4 enables the 16-bit ROM, bit 5 the bandwidth threshold, bit 6 a test mode and bit 7 VRAM.
A write computes the emulated memory mask from bits 0-1 and 3 of the byte, not a bus width.
The same write uses bit 3 as 256K rather than 64K chips and computes the mask from bits 0-1 and 3; bit 2 does nothing.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the ROM, threshold, test and VRAM bits change nothing.
TS Indexed Register 6, TS State Control, is read/write at port 3C5 and protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bits 1-2 with bit 0 of the TS Mode register select 9, 8, 10, 11, 12 or 16 dots per character in text mode.
Every CRTC character timing calculation except the 9-dot one treats the character as 8 dots wide.
Any write is stored and read back; the character width is not changed.
TS Indexed Register 7, TS Auxiliary Mode, is read/write at port 3C5 and protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bit 0 selects MCLK/4 and bit 1 divides the SCLK input frequency by two.
Bits 3 and 5 select the BIOS ROM address map and bits 2 and 4 are always set to 1.
Bit 6 divides MCLK by two and bit 7 enables VGA compatibility rather than EGA.
Any write is stored and read back; neither clock division is applied.
Any write is stored and read back; the ROM address map is not changed.
Any write is stored and read back; the mode stays as it was.
ATC Indexed Register 16, Miscellaneous, is read/write, read at 3C1 and written at 3C0, protected by the KEY.
The register is read/write and can be read back.
Bits 4-5 select normal, high-resolution or 16-bit high-color mode.
Bit 6 selects a 2-byte character code on the ET4000 Rev. E and bit 7 bypasses the internal palette.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; the display mode is not changed by these bits.
A write stores the byte and a read answers it; neither the character code nor the palette bypass takes effect.
The Miscellaneous Output register is read/write, written at 3C2 and read at 3CC.
Bits 3-2 choose the clock rate: MCLK clock 1, 2, 3 or 4.
Bits 0-7 are the address select, RAM enable, clock select, reserved, page select and two retrace polarities; a hardware reset clears them.
Bit 0 set gives 3DX addresses and 3DA for Input Status 1, clear gives 3BX and 3BA; bit 1 enables display memory access.
The PEL mask register is read/write at port hex 03C6.
A write sets the PEL mask value.
A read returns the mask value.
With vga_enable_3C6_ramdac set, four reads switch the port to the HiColor command byte; any access to 03C7, 03C8 or 03C9 clears that.
Setting a mode writes 0A0h or 00h into the command byte; INT 10h AX=10F2h with BL=2 writes 0E0h.
Port hex 03C7 is written as the PEL read address and read as the DAC state.
A write sets the PEL read address.
A read returns the DAC state.
Each access clears the HiColor command mode and defers to the base DAC handler.
The PEL write address register is read/write at port hex 03C8.
A write sets the PEL write address.
A read answers the write address.
Each access clears the HiColor command mode and defers to the base DAC handler.
Before answering, the read clears the HiColor command mode; the answer itself comes from the base DAC handler.
The PEL data register is read/write at port hex 03C9.
A write goes to the PEL data register at port hex 03C9.
A read comes from the PEL data register at port hex 03C9.
Each access clears the HiColor command mode and defers to the base DAC handler.
Before answering, the read clears the HiColor command mode; the answer itself comes from the base DAC handler.

A write stores the whole byte and changes no attribute.
A read answers the byte last stored.

rows.text: CRTC index 3Fh is handled by the ET4000 write and read handlers; its comment gives bits 0, 2, 4 and 7 as bit 8 of four registers.
A write stores the byte, keeps bits 0, 2 and 4 in a horizontal overflow field and triggers a resize when bits 0-1 change.
A read answers the byte last stored.

A write stores the byte, puts bit 1 into display start bit 16 and bit 0 into cursor start bit 16.
A read answers the byte last stored.

rows.text: CRTC index 24h, the compatibility control, is handled by the ET3000 write and read handlers.
A write stores the whole byte; bit 1 is read and written as clock-select 2 by the ET3000 clock helpers, and the other bits change nothing.
A read answers the byte last stored.
